standard_prerequisites: Chapter lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure (source lemma, worklist row 15): for any algebraic extension M of F there is a morphism of F-extensions M into a given algebraic closure
Chapter lemma-algebraic-goes-up (source lemma, worklist row 93): images of algebraic elements under an F-homomorphism are algebraic
Chapter lemma-algebraically-closed (worklist row 13): an algebraically closed field has no irreducible polynomials beyond the linear ones, hence admits no proper algebraic extension
core_obligations: The map phi: M ->  ar{F} from the map-into-algebraic-closure lemma is injective because M is a field, so phi(M) is isomorphic to M as an F-extension and hence algebraically closed
The extension phi(M) \subset  ar{F} is algebraic by lemma-algebraic-goes-up (every element of  ar{F} algebraic over F is algebraic over the subfield phi(M))
Since phi(M) is algebraically closed, every element of  ar{F} algebraic over phi(M) has a linear minimal polynomial over phi(M) and already lies in phi(M); hence  ar{F} = phi(M)
proof_roadmap: Land an F-map into the second closure and observe the image is an algebraically closed copy
Force equality through the no-proper-algebraic-extension corollary
